title: Aramco CEO: Hormuz Crisis May Haunt Oil Markets Until 2027
excerpt: Amin Nasser warns a prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure would delay global oil market recovery well into next year, as Q1 profits surge 25%.
body:
Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser delivered a stark warning on Monday: if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed past mid-June, the global oil market will not return to normal until 2027 — a timeline that would touch every corner of the world economy.

**What Nasser said on the Q1 earnings call:**
Speaking to investors, Nasser laid out a two-track scenario. Even an immediate reopening of Hormuz would take 'a few months for the market to rebalance.' A delay of even a few more weeks, he cautioned, pushes normalization into 2027. The scale of the damage is already staggering — the market has lost more than one billion barrels due to the closure, with a net loss of around 880 million barrels after accounting for redirected exports and strategic reserve releases.

**Why the global tanker fleet matters:**
Nasser identified tanker fleet dislocation as the single biggest challenge: ships are 'mixed up' in the wrong places. The closure costs the market 100 million barrels of supply every week Hormuz stays shut. Gasoline and jet fuel inventories are drawing down rapidly, with Nasser warning that levels 'may reach critically low levels ahead of the summer driving and travel season.' Aramco has ramped its East-West pipeline to maximum capacity of 7 million barrels per day to divert crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, but volumes there remain below pre-war levels. Meanwhile, Aramco's adjusted net income rose 26% to $33.6 billion in Q1 2026, as higher crude prices and the pipeline workaround offset export losses.

**What to watch:**
With US-Iran ceasefire talks on life support, all eyes turn to whether Hormuz reopens before the critical mid-June deadline Nasser identified — the line between months of disruption and years of it.
